261680206_7e4a2ca6.text: In our material, the EPD expresses selectively Calb1/CB, Otp, Pax6/PAX6, and Tbr1/TBR1, and its cells show a glutamatergic profile (consistent with our topographic description associating it to the paraventricular area); there are other specific molecular markers of EPD, such as Cyp26b1, Nos1, and Sst (Table 3; (Puelles et al., 2020)
261680206_7e4a2ca6.section: Developmental origin and related paraventricular-area context

261680206_6f31328a.text: .CB and Otp are markers shared by the supraoptic and paraventricular nuclei, which also derive from the paraventricular area (Pa; Díaz & Puelles, 2020;(Díaz et al., 2015)(Morales-Delgado et al., 2010), 2014;(Puelles et al., 2015). The Pa ventricular zone expresses PAX6 at early stages and sharply lacks expression of the Dlx1/2/5/6 or Nkx2-1 genes, which are otherwise present in the neighboring subpallial, preoptic, and subparaventricular domains. As noted above, the EPD cells generally express Slc17a6, a gene that encodes the VGLUT2 transporter, indicating a glutamatergic nature (see (Puelles et al., 2015). These findings on the EPD neurons are consistent with a possible origin within the paraventricular (Pa) histogenetic area corresponding specifically to the peduncular (hp1-derived) alar hypothalamus (Díaz & Puelles, 2020;(Puelles et al., 2003)(Puelles et al., 2015)(Puelles et al., 2015). However, we cannot exclude that additional Tbr1/TBR1-positive neurons may have migrated tangentially into the EPD locus from the caudally adjoining Tbr1-positive prethalamic eminence area.
